clue.text: Navy clubs, two different ones, ousting English group

parts.note: a navy is a fleet of ships
two kinds of club are needed: a wood (a golf club) and a mace (a heavy war club)

indicators.note: ousting says one letter is thrown out of the second club

parts.note: two kinds of club are needed: a wood (a golf club) and a mace (a heavy war club)

explanation.surface: Someone describes golf clubs and naval clubs while an English band gets pushed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs, two different ones' supplies both WOOD and MACE; 'ousting English' removes the E from MACE, leaving MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood Mac is a famous rock band, so the clue's word for a musical ensemble defines it.

clue.text: Reportedly strip a composer

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read, giving a near-sound

parts.note: a list is a strip of cloth, especially the selvage edge

explanation.surface: A composer is rumoured to be undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' looks like a verb but is a noun: a narrow band of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer.

clue.text: Record company bars head of department that's gone away

parts.note: EMI is a British record label
a grate is a set of bars

indicators.note: head of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A record company shuts out a departmental head who has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like a verb meaning excludes, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To have moved abroad to live is to have left one's country, departed for good.

clue.text: Flier need to reach FBI operative

parts.note: to win means to reach or attain, as in winning the shore
a G-man is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A pilot must rendezvous with an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who flies beside and protects the lead aircraft in formation is a flier.

clue.text: Extremes of climate varied with cloud cover

indicators.note: varied means altered, so the combined letters are rearranged
extremes of means the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Climate extremes bring changeable cloud cover.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the ends of 'climate', joins CLOUD and 'varied' shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or close off, which a lid or shield does.

clue.text: Change narcotic that's repeatedly cut

indicators.note: repeatedly cut says letters are removed from the end again and again, three times here

parts.note: morphine is a narcotic painkiller

explanation.surface: A drug has been diluted over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To morph is to transform smoothly from one shape into another, a kind of alteration.

clue.text: Separately go in to check disease

indicators.note: separately says the two letters of the word go are put in at different places
in to says the letters go inside the word for check

parts.note: to contain is to check or restrain
the word go supplies its two letters one at a time
the word go supplies its two letters one at a time

explanation.surface: An instruction to go in one at a time and check for disease.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes in after CONTA and O after I, giving CONTA-G-I-O-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagion is a disease spread by contact, so it is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Drunken actor, he trips into this?

definitions.text: Drunken actor, he trips into this?

indicators.note: drunken means staggering about, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tipsy performer stumbles off stage into the musicians' area.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunken area in front of a stage where musicians play is exactly where a falling actor would land.

clue.text: World-class footballer, one in charge of expected champion

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the Argentinian footballer
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A star footballer is cast as the saviour everyone was waiting for.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of expected champion' describes something relating to the awaited deliverer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messiah is the awaited saviour or champion, and the adjective describes anything relating to that figure.

clue.text: It stops a walrus getting wet

definitions.text: It stops a walrus getting wet

parts.words: It stops a walrus getting wet
parts.note: a walrus is also a thick drooping moustache; this cup has a ledge to keep it dry while drinking

explanation.surface: Something keeps an Arctic animal dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walrus' is the bushy moustache style, not the sea mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian drinking vessel with a guard across the rim protects facial hair from tea.

clue.text: Service break

parts.note: in military slang, leave from duty in the armed services is rest and recreation

explanation.surface: A tennis player breaks an opponent's serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis sense of a break of serve misleads; 'Service' means the armed forces, and the answer is their term for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest and recreation is the military phrase for time off granted to troops, a break from the services.

clue.text: Out-and-out maniac losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the slang word for maniac is dropped

parts.note: a nutter is slang for a madman

explanation.surface: A total lunatic loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are intensifying adjectives meaning complete or absolute, as in an utter fool.

clue.text: Trap oar blade that's rubbish

parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'
wash is an old word for the flat blade of an oar

explanation.surface: A rower dismisses a blade as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the 'oar blade' sense and the 'rubbish' sense are dictionary rarities.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is listed in Chambers as slang for nonsense or empty talk, like hogwash.

clue.text: Town's sympathetic woman in fashion

indicators.note: in says the woman is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton means fashion or style, as in bon ton
an agony aunt is a woman who gives sympathetic advice

explanation.surface: A town's kindly lady is very fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a real English county town, so the bare word for a settlement defines it.

clue.text: Acting together, peacekeepers quelling hostility about nothing

indicators.note: quelling means sitting on top of, so in this down entry the peacekeepers come first

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: about says the hostility surrounds the zero

parts.note: animus means hostility or ill will
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers jointly suppress pointless hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone agrees completely they act as one, with no dissent.

clue.text: Unnamed swearing loony listens in furtively

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the remaining letters are rearranged
unnamed says the abbreviation N for name is removed from the next word

explanation.surface: An anonymous foul-mouthed lunatic eavesdrops.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N (name) from SWEARING to leave SWEARIG, which 'loony' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is a British informal verb for eavesdropping on someone's conversation.

clue.text: One artist holding another back finally gets towards the back

indicators.note: back says the combined artists are read in reverse
holding says the first artist contains the second

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist
another artist: RA, a Royal Academician

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: One artist restrains another and ends up at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW-RA-ER, read 'back', gives RE-AR-WARD; the last letter of 'gets' adds S.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in the direction behind, towards the rear.

clue.text: Czech Republic party with branch outside eastern empire

parts.note: CZ is the international code for the Czech Republic

indicators.note: outside says the branch goes around the party

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a tree or organisation
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A Czech celebration spreads into an eastern empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The realm ruled by a Russian emperor was a Slavic empire in the east of Europe.

clue.text: Unfeminine minute woman gains his fancy

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny woman wins the man's affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a woman as having masculine traits is the opposite of feminine.

clue.text: Brief period in which bad weather stops coach

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the weather sits inside the shortened period
brief says the word for period is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as at school
rain is a kind of bad weather

explanation.surface: A short spell of rain halts a coach journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus, but it is the sports sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach and a trainer are both people who instruct athletes.

clue.text: One may follow another dainty clipped bird

parts.note: twee means excessively dainty or quaint

indicators.note: clipped says the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A dainty bird with clipped wings trails behind another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to following accounts on Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Twitter user may follow another user's posts, so the social media sense fits.

clue.text: Being sixteen, happy and extremely carefree

indicators.note: happy is used in the sense of drunk or tipsy, so the letters are jumbled
extremely means take only the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A carefree sixteen-year-old enjoys life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy' rearranges SIXTEEN into EXISTEN; the ends of 'carefree' add CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being, as a noun, means the state of being alive or real, the same as existing.

clue.text: At last, Hewitt wears hat for championship

indicators.note: wears says the letter is inside the hat, as a head is under it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the tennis player's name

explanation.surface: Tennis player Lleyton Hewitt wears a hat for the championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the status of being champion, as in winning a world title.

clue.text: Cheer a doctor before surgical procedure

indicators.note: before puts the doctor ahead of the procedure

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC's time-travelling hero
op is short for an operation

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a cheer before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of joy, so it is a kind of cheer.

clue.text: Sports champion pulled up in strike zone

indicators.note: pulled up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A baseball champion is hauled up in the strike zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters; 'pulled up' reverses them in this down entry. The answer is a top sumo rank.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the second-highest rank in sumo wrestling, held by champion-level wrestlers.

clue.text: Means of fixing the fastest-ever human

definitions.meaning: a bolt bent into a U shape with threaded ends, used to clamp things
the sprinter Usain Bolt, reduced to his initial and surname

explanation.surface: A record sprinter is described as a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition shortens Usain to his initial U.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hardware fastener for pipes and posts, so 'means of fixing' is a fair general description.

clue.text: Cross between nearly all denominations

parts.note: inter is a Latin word for between, familiar from words like interval

indicators.note: nearly all says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: religious denominations are sects

explanation.surface: A cross stands between nearly all church denominations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the Christian symbol, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a line or road means to cut across it, as two lines meeting do.

clue.text: Food guide discovered in abridged format

parts.note: a shepherd guides a flock

indicators.note: abridged format means shortened, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: spied means discovered or spotted

explanation.surface: A guidebook is found in a shortened edition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato, so food covers it.
